item.text: {"gaps":[{"concept":"Preeclampsia thresholds: blood pressure ≥140/90 mm Hg and proteinuria ≥300 mg/day or protein:creatinine ratio ≥0.3; severe hypertension is ≥160/110.","why_tested":"A vignette gives exact blood pressure and urine values and asks for the diagnosis or severity.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Chronic hypertension with new proteinuria or organ dysfunction after 20 weeks indicates superimposed preeclampsia.","why_tested":"A patient with hypertension before pregnancy develops new findings in the third trimester.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Major preeclampsia risk factors include prior preeclampsia, first pregnancy, multifetal gestation, chronic hypertension, kidney disease, diabetes, and molar pregnancy.","why_tested":"A stem asks which pregnant patient is most likely to develop preeclampsia.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Preeclampsia causes glomerular endotheliosis: swollen glomerular endothelial cells narrow capillary lumens and produce proteinuria.","why_tested":"A renal biopsy or mechanism question accompanies hypertension and proteinuria in pregnancy.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"HELLP hemolysis is microangiopathic, with schistocytes, elevated LDH, and indirect bilirubin.","why_tested":"A pregnant patient has right upper quadrant pain, thrombocytopenia, and fragmented red cells.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Preeclampsia and eclampsia can first present after delivery.","why_tested":"A recently postpartum patient develops severe headache, hypertension, visual symptoms, or seizures.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Gestational diabetes risk factors include obesity, prior gestational diabetes or macrosomic infant, polycystic ovary syndrome, and family history of diabetes.","why_tested":"A stem asks which patient warrants early diabetes screening or has the highest risk.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"High-risk patients may be tested for previously unrecognized diabetes at the first prenatal visit; routine gestational screening remains at 24–28 weeks.","why_tested":"A patient with major diabetes risk factors presents early in pregnancy and the question asks when to test.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Maternal glucose crosses the placenta, but maternal insulin does not; fetal hyperglycemia stimulates fetal pancreatic β-cell hyperplasia.","why_tested":"A question asks why maternal diabetes causes fetal overgrowth and neonatal hypoglycemia.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Fetal hyperinsulinemia delays surfactant production, increasing neonatal respiratory distress despite macrosomia.","why_tested":"A large infant of a diabetic mother develops respiratory distress shortly after birth.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Diabetic embryopathy follows hyperglycemia during organogenesis; diabetes first developing late in pregnancy does not cause those early structural defects.","why_tested":"A question contrasts congenital malformations in pregestational diabetes with complications of gestational diabetes.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Maternal diabetic vasculopathy can cause placental insufficiency and fetal growth restriction despite diabetes’ usual association with macrosomia.","why_tested":"A patient with longstanding diabetes and vascular disease has a growth-restricted fetus.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Transvaginal ultrasound identifies placenta previa by placental coverage of the internal cervical os.","why_tested":"A patient with painless third-trimester bleeding needs a test to locate the placenta.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Accreta attaches to myometrium, increta invades myometrium, and percreta penetrates through serosa, sometimes reaching the bladder.","why_tested":"A pathology or imaging stem asks for the depth of abnormal placental invasion.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Placenta accreta spectrum may show placental lacunae and loss of the normal placental–myometrial interface on ultrasound.","why_tested":"A patient with prior cesarean delivery and previa has a characteristic prenatal ultrasound.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Placental abruption may cause concealed hemorrhage; external bleeding can underestimate blood loss and shock.","why_tested":"A patient has severe abdominal pain and a rigid uterus with little visible bleeding.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Vasa previa is associated with velamentous cord insertion or a succenturiate placental lobe;
